thesis: A calendar audit is proposed to distinguish reactive management from creation, learning, and thinking.
summary: The source divides professional time into four categories and asks the viewer to color-code a week in half-hour increments. It then recommends protecting creation and making room for consumption and ideation. Selected passages support the procedure; broad claims about dopamine, typical time use, or guaranteed growth remain unverified. The note records a diagnostic exercise rather than a proven productivity treatment.
